definitions.explanation: A woman on her wedding day or about to be married.
A married woman (from the perspective of her husband or his family).

examples.english: To get married (said of a woman).
examples.notes: 嫁に行く = to marry into another family

examples.japanese: お{嫁|よめ}さんがきれいだった。
{娘|むすめ}を{嫁|よめ}に{出|だ}す{日|ひ}が{来|き}た。
examples.english: The day has come to send our daughter off as a bride.
examples.notes: 嫁に出す = to send one's daughter off in marriage

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{来年|らいねん}お{嫁|よめ}さんになる{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: She is planning to become a bride next year.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さい{頃|ころ}、「{大|おお}きくなったらお{嫁|よめ}さんになりたい」と{言|い}っていた。
examples.english: When she was little, she used to say, 'I want to be a bride when I grow up.'

examples.japanese: うちの{嫁|よめ}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: My wife is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}の{嫁|よめ}が{来月|らいげつ}{来|く}る。
examples.english: My son's wife is coming next month.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}を{嫁|よめ}にもらった。
examples.english: I took her as my wife.
examples.notes: 嫁にもらう = to take as a wife (traditional expression)

examples.japanese: {嫁|よめ}と{姑|しゅうとめ}の{関係|かんけい}がうまくいかないことがある。
examples.english: The relationship between a wife and mother-in-law sometimes doesn't go well.
examples.notes: 嫁と姑 = wife and mother-in-law (common topic in Japanese culture)

examples.japanese: {嫁|よめ}さんのことを{友達|ともだち}に{自慢|じまん}するのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: He likes to brag about his wife to his friends.

notes:
USAGE: {嫁|よめ} can mean (1) bride, (2) wife (casual/informal), or (3) daughter-in-law. The meaning depends on context and the speaker's perspective.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{嫁|よめ}に{行|い}く (to get married - for women)
・{嫁|よめ}にもらう (to take as a wife)
・{嫁|よめ}さん (wife - casual/affectionate)
・お{嫁|よめ}さん (bride)

RELATED:
・{花嫁|はなよめ} - bride (at wedding)
・{婿|むこ} - groom, son-in-law
・{妻|つま} - wife (formal)
